name: Gwen Stefani
notes: Post-band pop on hip-hop and 80s-electro rhythm beds, and the sparsest drum block in this section by design: "deliberately sparse drum-machine kit — kick on 1 and 3, huge clap/snare on 2&4, no hats for whole sections… the beat *is* the arrangement". That last clause is what the model encodes hardest — `hihat.continuous` is false with a fill density of 0.1, which is what "no hats for whole sections" means to the generator, and the clap/snare accent tier is the loudest here. The "marching-band snare and brass added as the 'fill'" is the snare-roll ladder plus a tom lane. Harmony is a documented two-chord alternation between B major and D-sharp minor — VI to i "with voice-leading rather than a cadence" — so `maxChords` is 2, the vamp carries the harmonic rhythm and no family contains a V. The low end is "a single low synth/808-style tone on the root, long and undecorated; the space under the beat is left open"; it is described as a *tone* under a synth palette rather than a trap 808 line, so no `bass808` block is authored and the bassline runs `mirror_kick` at 0.98 with the register kept low and tight. The topline is "chant not melody — cheerleader call-and-response on 2 or 3 pitches, with the hook shouted in unison", which is `motifPitchCount` 2–3 — the entry's own count, floor included — over a `call_response` structure. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are the drum probabilities and the melody density; the entry gives a pitch count and a delivery, not a note count. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“a single low synth/808-style tone on the root, long and undecorated; the space under the beat is left open.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord. ⚠ **`anticipationProb` 0.06 → 0.18 is the only bassline change, and `followRootsProb` 0.98 is deliberately untouched.** The research is *"a single low synth/808-style tone on the root, long and undecorated; the space under the beat is left open"* — undecorated means the pitch does not move, so the movement had to come from placement rather than from notes. It measured **768 of 1,000 distinct basslines** against `bass.rs`'s 0.95 saturation share, over a kick that is fixed on 1, 3 and `3&` at every seed. ⚠ **INFERRED:** 0.18 is a lane-conventional rate for an 80s-electro drum-machine bed, not a sourced one. ⛔ The bassline declares `loopVerbatim`: the entry says "a single low synth/808-style tone on the root, long and undecorated; the space under the beat is left open", so this low end is static by description rather than thin by accident. `engine/tests/bass.rs::static_low_end` waives the saturation share for it and nothing else — the absolute floor of 500 distinct basslines still applies and this model clears it. The declaration needs the corroborating `followRootsProb` of 0.98 beside it, so the word alone could not buy the exemption.
